issues.description: Class constructor mismatch for de.tum.cit.ase.Farm: the problem statement (and example usage in the template Main) require a no-argument constructor Farm() that initializes the internal ArrayList of animals, but the solution repository only provides a single constructor Farm(int initialCapacity). The template Farm.java also does not provide a constructor. This inconsistency will cause code or tests that call new Farm() (as shown in the template Main) to fail to compile and will confuse students about which constructor to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a public no-argument constructor to Farm that initializes the animals list (for example: public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }). Optionally keep the existing Farm(int initialCapacity) constructor as an overload. Alternatively, if the design intentionally requires an initial capacity parameter, update the problem statement and template Main to use Farm(int initialCapacity) and document the change.
